distinguishing_features: A compliant elastomer layer/liner is placed at the elbow impingement site rather than changing upstream impact conditions.
The mechanism reduces transmitted peak contact stress by increasing collision duration and viscoelastic energy absorption.
The wear mode is shifted from direct metal abrasive cutting/fatigue to sacrificial elastomer erosion.
The implementation uses a bonded or clipped polyurethane layer on the base metal wall.
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to protect a pneumatic conveying elbow from wear-through under high-velocity particle impingement by reducing the damaging impact energy delivered to the metal wall.
parsed.viable_reason: A bonded 2 mm polyurethane liner is a practical, testable construction that can reduce metal impingement wear by providing a sacrificial compliant layer, although the numerical support is approximate.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Prior art 2 already targets impact-induced liner wear by reducing impact energy flux, and using a known elastomer/PU wear liner instead of hard-facing is a routine protective measure.
